text: `new BufferedInputStream(new GZIPInputStream(raw))` composes behavior by wrapping rather than subclassing. What does that buy?
choices: Only a wrapper can be closed independently of the stream it decorates.
One buffering class works for files, sockets and decompressors, instead of a method for every combination.
Wrapping avoids the virtual dispatch cost that inheritance would impose on each read.
Subclassing is forbidden for JDK classes, so decoration is the only mechanism available.
explanation: It is Section 23.1.2's argument in the standard library: `BufferedInputStream` holds an `InputStream` rather than extending `FileInputStream`, so it can buffer a socket. The alternative would be `readGzippedUtf8FileWithBuffering` and every other combination. The library chose composability over convenience and then spent twenty years adding convenience — `Files.readString` and `Files.lines` — on top.
